scope: Proposition 7.3 (Hilbert products through length four) of the manuscript “Scale and conformal symmetry in four-dimensional operational quantum field theory” (preprints/Scale-and-conformal-symmetry-in-four-dimensional-operational-quantum-field-theory-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 282 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 485a44682f95ef0d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For entries from t, S, V, L, and hence J, ℓ and their derivatives, there are Hilbert-valued product distributions on mutually spacelike real patches through total length four. They are multilinear, permutation-symmetric, and covariant under translations, Lorentz transformations and dilations. They satisfy every leg-local linear identity of their vacuum waves. With C in a common opposite cone, they obey ⟨CΩ, Ψ[O1 · · · Op]⟩ = D O† 1Ω, C∗ Ψ[O2 · · · Op] E . (7.5) Smearings on the left side of the inner product are conjugated. The scalar functions factor at every split of total length at most four. Explicitly, for p + q ≤ 4 and both words in their vector tubes, Ψ[A1(z1) · · · Ap(zp)], Ψ[B1(w1) · · · Bq(wq)] = W A† p(z̄p), . . . , A† 1(z̄1), B1(w1), . . . , Bq(wq)  . (7.6) Here an empty word is Ω, and bra source tests are conjugated and reversed. The reversed bra gaps, the ket gaps, and the central gap Im w1 + Im z1 are all future directed. Thus the scalar word is in its gap-only tube. In particular the case p = q = 2 gives the pair–pair Gram identities. All these products extend holomorphically to (7.2) and the spacelike tie neighborhoods of Proposition 6.7; the split identities persist wherever both vector factors are defined.
